lina (support): Alert from monitoring: hosted inference 503 spike in us-west-2 since ~03:12 UTC. Multiple customers reporting request timeouts and 5xx. https://grafana.example/redwood/alerts/823 :rotating_light:
benj (oncall): seeing +12% 5xx at the gateway, p95 latency up 2s. Top upstream is infer-host-12 for model rtx-large-quant. Routing shows many requests pinned there after yesterday's model swap.
eva (sre): grabbing logs from infer-host-12. initial glance shows repeated OOM + segfaults during hot-prefetch. attaching snippet.
ops-bot: log: /var/log/infer-runner/12345.log uploaded: https://s3.redwood/logs/7192223334/infer-runner-12345.log
eva (sre): ```
[2026-03-17T03:14:21Z] infer-runner(12345): CUDA malloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-17T03:14:22Z] infer-runner(12345): Exception: segfault at 0x7f2a3d0
pid=12345 signal=SIGSEGV
Backtrace: 0x400f12 0x4012ab 0x7f2a3d0
```
mike (infra): those hosts got the quant-swap from last night (quant-v2). Repro rate looks correlated with long context sessions + concurrent streaming.
tara (customer-success): one paying customer (AcmeHealth) opened a support ticket — they saw 503 on critical invoices endpoint. They're asking for ETA and workaround.
benj (oncall): quick mitigation: 1) update routing to avoid infer-host-12 by draining it; 2) temporarily pin high-risk customers to fp16 variant; 3) lower max-concurrency for rtx-large-quant. Can we push fast?
eva (sre): draining now. `kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/infer-host-12 -n hosted-usw2` (doing graceful drain). Also pushing a hotfix to disable quant-prefetch buffer on that pool.
mike (infra): applied routing change: traffic->fallback-pool. Confirming reduction in 5xx.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback triggered: model-catalog/rtx-large-quant -> rtx-large-fp16 at 03:20 UTC by evading-rollback-job
benj (oncall): customer update drafted: "We're routing you to a stable variant while we investigate; no billing impact expected." tara to send.
tara (customer-success): sent to AcmeHealth, they acknowledged but asked for root cause.
eva (sre): repro notes: stress test on a replica with concurrent streaming + context=32k triggers OOM within ~30s after quant prefetch. Might be prefetch thrashing kernel allocations. Repro script: `python tools/loadtest.py --model rtx-large-quant --concurrency 40 --context 32000 --streaming`
benj (oncall): next actions: collect coredump from infer-runner on host, gather dmesg, nvml logs, and exact allocator traces. Assigning to mike to capture GPU mem maps.
mike (infra): grabbing coredump now. Commands I'm running: `sudo gdb -c /var/crash/core.12345 /opt/infer/bin/runner` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0 > /tmp/gpu-mem-7192223334.txt`.
eva (sre): tentative root cause: quantized prefetch path is allocating pinned host buffers aggressively; under high concurrency the driver free path races and leads to invalid access (SIGSEGV). If confirmed, plan: patch prefetch to bound pinned allocations, add KV cache backpressure, and revert quant swap for affected pool.
benj (oncall): severity remains P1 while customers impacted. Keeping channel open. Add postmortem owner.
tara (customer-success): AcmeHealth asked for timeline and whether to expect retries to succeed. Recommend we advise them to retry with exponential backoff; we're keeping them on fp16 fallback.
eva (sre): creating incident ticket INC-2026-0317-34 and will schedule a follow-up triage.
benj (oncall): thanks team. Quick note: after routing change 5xx rate dropped to baseline within 4m. Re-enable gradual traffic when patch ready. :white_check_mark:
